input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there

doc_friction.issue: Steps 1-2 lead to owner-gated work: both open perf backlog items are owner rows, and the four heaviest workflows in the pool reading (CodeQL, Security gate, Portfolio Pages, CI policy) are all priv-*. Only Portfolio validate was left as a CI target.
It proves a sparse tree gives the same answers, but says nothing about speed. blob:none plus a near-full sparse set is slower than a plain checkout. A note now says so.

deviations.why: The prompt expects a speed-up to land. The measured change was no faster (44-49 s vs 43 s), so I reverted it and landed the cost model, P086 and a post section instead.
deviations.did: reverted the workflow edit in the same PR
deviations.result: no CI change; the negative result is written down with numbers so the next run doesn't repeat it

notes: Metric: Portfolio validate checkout step seconds. Before: 44 s median (n=34, ci_profile.py --runs 600 --save, step durations), one job's log 32 s fetch + 11 s write = 43 s. After, blob:none + /* !/research/: 49 s (PR 19072, run 45685975017). After, also !*.mp3 !*.mp4: 44 s (run 45687819913). Locally (fetch --depth=1 + checkout via the proxy): full 54 s, blob:none no-research 94 s, blob:limit=512k 57 s, blob:none no-research-no-media 53 s. Equivalence: all 106 steps ran in the full and sparse trees with the same rc, test counts and last lines (strace of the full run showed no step opens research/ or media). Cost model: lazy blob fetch about 0.7 ms per file whatever the size; it pays only well under about 50k files. Change reverted. Filed owner-gated P086 (conflict-markers keeps 79.6k files with blob:none, 48 s vs 43 s full).

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing page (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing), fetched 2026-11-12. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads are 0.1x input except 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 and 0.025x on Fable/Mythos 5.1 and 5.2. Sonnet 5.5 cache_read was 0.20 here until 2026-11-12 (quality audit round 48): records priced before then overstate Sonnet 5.5 cost.

human_equivalent.basis: tracing 106 CI steps, two CI experiments and fetch timings by hand

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
